rydberg.photoionization_note: Two 229 nm photons exceed the ionization energy: resonant two-photon ionization via 5s5p 1P1 limits 229 nm MOTs (cross section under levels[5s5p 1P1].photoionization). Yamaguchi et al. calculate a 2 mHz three-photon ionization rate of the clock state in the 420 nm magic lattice (theory).

not_found: Laser-measured absolute frequency of the 332 nm 1S0-3P0 clock line (111Cd, 113Cd): Yamaguchi et al. PRL 123, 113201 (2019) (arXiv:1909.07931, opened) report narrow-line cooling, clock-line spectroscopy and the magic wavelength but print no absolute clock frequency; Schelfhout & McFerran 2022 mention unpublished RIKEN values (private communication). Only the Burns & Adams 1956 level value and theory predictions are given.
Measured lifetime of 5s5p 3P0 (hyperfine-quenched) in 111Cd / 113Cd: only Garstang's 1962 calculation (7.0 / 7.6 mHz) quoted by Yamaguchi et al.

Measured lifetimes of 5s6s 3S1 and 5s5d 3D1,2,3 (Xu et al., Phys. Rev. A 70, 042508 (2004) is the usual reference; paywalled, not opened). Only the linewidths quoted in cold-atom papers (3S1 ~17.5-18 MHz, 361 nm line 23-25 MHz) are recorded.
Hyperfine constants of 5s5d 3D1, 3D2 and of 5s6p states for 111Cd / 113Cd (omitted in Gibble's table).
Measured Lande g factors of Cd I excited states: none located (NIST ASD levels file has none for these levels).
Isotope shifts of the 467.8 nm (3P0-3S1) and 508.6 nm (3P2-3S1) lines: Wenz et al. 1981 and Hammen et al. are cited by Ohayon et al. but their numbers are not printed there.
Measured branching ratios of 5s6s 3S1 -> 3P0,1,2 and 5s5d 3D -> 3P: only NIST ASD A values (accuracy C-D).
conflicts: 229 nm isotope shifts: Hofsaess et al. 2023 (quantum-interference line-shape model, enriched targets) vs Tinsley et al. 2021 (beam): 106-114 1818.1 vs 1748(11) MHz, 110-114 865.0 vs 826(6) MHz etc.; Hofsaess kept.

229 nm absolute frequency of 114Cd: 1309 864 341(20) MHz (Hofsaess) vs 1309 864 580(86) MHz (Burns & Adams 1956, 3 sigma) vs 1309 864 506(262) MHz (Tinsley). 326 nm: 919 046 234(21) vs 919 046 357(42) MHz (Burns & Adams).

5s5p 1P1 lifetime: 1.60(5) ns (linewidth, Hofsaess 2023) vs 1.75(20) ns (Xu 2004), 1.66(5) ns (Hanle, 1964/1969), 1.90(15) ns (beam foil), theory 1.514(15) ns; historic range 1.11-2.3 ns. NIST ASD A = 5.3e8 s^-1 corresponds to 1.89 ns.
1P1 hyperfine splitting of 113Cd: 295.6(3.4) MHz (Hofsaess) vs 251(5) MHz (Tinsley 2021).

326 nm centre-of-gravity shift 111-114: 861.6(1.0) MHz (Gibble 2024, MOT) vs 857.2(0.4 stat + 3.3 sys) MHz (Hofsaess 2023); bosons: MOT-edge values (Ohayon) are 2-5 MHz above the beam values, within the 3.3 MHz systematic.
5s5p 3P1 lifetime: 2.39(4) us (Byron 1964) vs weighted mean of all measurements 2.30(10) us; NIST ASD A = 4.06e5 s^-1 corresponds to 2.46 us.
361 nm line width: 25 MHz (Gibble 2024) vs 23 MHz (Ohayon 2022) vs 20.7 MHz from the NIST A value.
notes: Conventions. (1) Isotope-shift keys 'a-b' mean nu(a) - nu(b); all Cd shifts are relative to 114Cd as printed. Fermion shifts are hyperfine centres of gravity. (2) Hyperfine entries carry the measured interval (interval_MHz) and a derived A_MHz; I = 1/2 so B = 0. (3) Fields beyond SCHEMA.md: natural_linewidth_*, interval_MHz, photoionization, magic_wavelength_nm, bbr_shift_Hz, type 'M2', top-level 'rydberg' (ionization limit) and 'conflicts'. (4) rme_J_ea0 values are derived here from measured lifetimes with the schema convention (branching to the ground state taken as 1); they are not printed in the sources. (5) The clock (332 nm) and 314 nm isotope shifts are King-plot derived values of Ohayon et al., not direct measurements.
